newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway central bank plans first repo auction.
newsitem.headline: Norway central bank plans first repo auction.

text.p: Norway's central bank, Norges Bank, said on Tuesday it would introduce for the first time repurchase agreements for government bonds and treasury bills to supply liquidity to the money market.
The bank said the 13-day operation would run from February 20 to March 4 and would be held by Dutch auction.
The arrangement covers government bonds S462, S466, S463, S465 and S467. Also included are T-bills SS42, SS46, SS43, SS44 and SS45.
Banks may submit three bids for rates, minimum volume is 25 million crowns, Norges Bank said.

Norway normally uses fixed-rate loans and desposits to control money market liquidity. A bank spokesman said the repo instrument was being introduced to introduce an element of collateral for money distributed into the banking system.
But, he said, Norges Bank did not expect to use repos often. More likely the bank would be forced to drain liquidity from the market.
"We are not expecting to do this often. It's a special situation when liquidity is so low we think it's the right thing to do at this moment," the spokesman said.

He attributed the lack of liquidity in the money market to corporate value-added-tax payments and to payments by state oil company Den norske stats oljeselskap AS to the government for its share of the country's oil production.
